elements.element: Transition assistance obligation on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "provide reasonable transition assistance" upon "expiry or termination"

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
Assistance priced at Vendor's then-current rates
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export" — the clock runs from a Customer request, not from expiry or termination

elements.element: Customer Data returned in a standard machine-readable format
Deletion of Customer Data after return
elements.evidence: "thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems"

elements.element: At least 90 days of transition assistance
elements.evidence: "for up to six (6) months" exceeds 90 days
"within thirty (30) days ... return or make available for export all Customer Data"

reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the 30-day data-return deadline is measured from "Customer's request" rather than from expiry or termination, so a request condition swallows the mandatory post-termination return deadline. Change to "within thirty (30) days of expiry or termination" (a request condition may remain for transition assistance only).

Minimality: extending the trigger to termination of "any Order Form" broadens scope beyond what the position requires; termination of a single Order Form would trigger return and deletion of all Customer Data while other Services continue.

Preserves intent: the Order Form-level trigger creates a conflict with continuing subscriptions and with Section 16.5/Sections 11 and 15 governance of Customer Data; the duty to delete "all Customer Data" on any single Order Form's expiry is a dangling mechanic.

The clause as drafted does sit at or above the fallback (six months' assistance, 30-day export, deletion certification), so only the return-trigger and Order Form scope need fixing to reach the locked preferred target.
